title: Year 6 end-of-year GPS check
subject: English
source: Written for english/y6 lesson 97 (Year 6 end-of-year GPS check: 30 grammar and punctuation questions and 20 spellings (teacher-written, in the portal and printable))
intro: Lesson 97. Sections A to C: 30 grammar and punctuation questions. Section D: 20 spellings read by the teacher.

questions.q: Rewrite in the passive: The scientists stored the seeds.
questions.a: The seeds were stored by the scientists.

questions.q: Underline the subordinate clause: Although it was dark, the vault was safe.
Add a semi-colon: The door was small the vault was huge.
questions.a: The door was small; the vault was huge.

questions.q: Add a colon to introduce the list: You need three things a pen, a ruler and paper.
questions.a: You need three things: a pen, a ruler and paper.

questions.q: Write in the subjunctive: If I (be) a scientist, I would study seeds.
questions.a: If I were a scientist, I would study seeds.

questions.q: Add brackets for parenthesis: Svalbard a group of islands is in Norway.
questions.a: Svalbard (a group of islands) is in Norway.

questions.q: Add dashes for parenthesis: The vault opened in 2008 after years of planning.
questions.a: The vault opened in 2008 - after years of planning. (accept dashes round 'after years of planning' only in a mid-sentence version)

questions.q: Underline the relative pronoun: The seeds, which came from Syria, were saved.
Which word is a modal verb? We should protect crops.
Add a hyphen: a well known scientist
Write the antonym of 'stable'.
Write a synonym for 'vital'.
Underline the fronted adverbial: Far to the north, a door pokes out of the snow.
Change to the past progressive: The snow falls.
Change to the present perfect: The vault stores seeds.
Add the missing apostrophe: the worlds crops
Add the missing apostrophe: the countries seeds (more than one country)
Is this a statement, question, command or exclamation? Store the seeds carefully.
Turn into a question with a question tag: The vault is cold.
questions.a: The vault is cold, isn't it?

questions.q: Which is the determiner? Every country owns its seeds.
Expand the noun phrase: the door
questions.a: For example: the narrow concrete door in the mountainside

questions.q: Use 'whose' to join: Scientists returned seeds. Their seed bank was damaged.
questions.a: Scientists whose seed bank was damaged returned seeds.

questions.q: Correct the verb: The seeds was kept cold.
Insert a comma to avoid confusion: Let's eat Grandad.
Formal or informal? 'Hey, check out this vault!'
Rewrite formally: We got loads of seeds.
questions.a: We received a large number of seeds.

questions.q: Add an adverbial of time: ___, the vault opened.
Which word is the conjunction? The seeds were safe because the ground was frozen.
Add a prefix: understand (to mean understand wrongly)
Add the bullet-point punctuation consistently: list three things stored in the vault.
questions.a: For example: rice; wheat; beans (consistent punctuation)
